import pandas as pd

# Define source file paths
source_files = [
    "autopipeline-benchmarks/github-pipelines/length4_54/training_0.csv",
    "autopipeline-benchmarks/github-pipelines/length4_54/training_1.csv",
    "autopipeline-benchmarks/github-pipelines/length4_54/training_2.csv",
    "autopipeline-benchmarks/github-pipelines/length4_54/training_3.csv"
]

# List to hold dataframes
dfs = []

# Load each source CSV file with index_col=0 to ignore the numerical index column
for file_path in source_files:
    df = pd.read_csv(file_path, index_col=0)
    # The source schema is ['WarNum', 'WhereFought'], but target schema is ['WhereFought', 'WarNum']
    # So reorder columns to match target schema
    df = df[['WhereFought', 'WarNum']]
    # Ensure columns are integer type as per target schema
    df['WhereFought'] = df['WhereFought'].astype(int)
    df['WarNum'] = df['WarNum'].astype(int)
    dfs.append(df)

# Since all source tables have the exact same schema as the target (same columns and types),
# we can union (concatenate) all source dataframes
target_df = pd.concat(dfs, ignore_index=True)

# Write the resulting dataframe to the target CSV file path
target_df.to_csv("autopipeline-benchmarks/github-pipelines/length4_54/target_multisource_cot.csv", index=False)

# UNION all source tables (concatenate)

# GROUP BY WhereFought and aggregate WarNum by min (to match target FD and reduce duplicates)
